old_text: No match is won unless played out or given up, except in the case provided in Law 45.
new_text: No match is won unless played out or given up, except in the case provided for in Law 45.

old_text: Before the commencemen of the match two umpires shall be appointed, one for each end.
new_text: Before the commencement of the match two umpires shall be appointed, one for each end.

old_text: The ball shall weigh no less than 5½oz., nor more than 5¾oz.
new_text: The ball shall weigh not less than 5½oz., nor more than 5¾oz.

old_text: It shall measure not less than 9in., nor more than 9¼in. in circumference.
new_text: It shall measure not less than 9in. nor more than 9¼in. in circumference.

old_text: The bat shall not exceed 4¼in. in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38in. in length.
new_text: The bat shall not exceed 4½ in. in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38in. in length.

old_text: The bails shall be each 4½in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.
new_text: The bails shall be each 4⅝in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.

old_text: The ground shall not be rolled, watered, covered, mown or beaten during a match, except before the commencement of each innings and of each day’s play; when, unless the in-side object, the ground shall be swept and rolled for not more than ten minutes.
new_text: The ground shall not be rolled, watered, covered, mown or beaten during a match, except before the commencement of each innings and of each day’s play, when, unless the in side object, the ground shall be swept and rolled for not more than ten minutes.

old_text: This shall not prevent the batsmen from beating the ground with his bat, nor the batsman or bowler from using sawdust in order to obtain a proper foothold.
new_text: This shall not prevent the batsman from beating the ground with his bat, nor the batsman nor bowler from using sawdust in order to obtain a proper foothold.

old_text: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked, the umpire shall call "No-ball.”
new_text: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked, the umpire shall call “No ball.”

old_text: The bowler shall deliver the ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling crease and within the return crease, otherwise the umpire shall call "No ball.”
new_text: The bowler shall deliver the ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling crease, and within the return crease, otherwise the umpire shall call “No Ball.”

old_text: Neither a "No-ball" nor a "Wide-ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “Over."
new_text: Neither a “No-ball” nor a “Wide ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “Over.”

old_text: The striker may hit a "no ball," and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a "noball,” unless he be run out or break Laws 26, 27, 29, 30.
new_text: The striker may hit a “no-ball," and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a “no-ball,” unless he be run out or break laws 26, 27, 29, 30.

old_text: From a wide ball as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as "wide balls,” and if no run be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.
new_text: From a “wide ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “wide balls,” and if no run be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.

old_text: If the ball, not having been called "wide" or "no ball," pass the striker, without touching his bat or person, and any runs be obtained, the umpire shall call "Bye,” but if the ball touch any part of the striker’s person (hand excepted), and any run be obtained, the umpire shall call "Leg bye,” such runs to be scored "byes” and "leg byes” respectively.
new_text: If the ball, not having been called “wide” or “no-ball,” pass the striker, without touching his bat, or person, and any runs be obtained, the umpire shall call “bye;” but if the ball touch any part of the striker’s person (hand excepted) and any run be obtained, the umpire shall call “leg-bye,” such runs to be scored “byes” and “leg-byes” respectively.

old_text: At the beginning of the match, and of each innings, the umpire at the bowler’s wicket shall call "Play”; from that time no trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out, the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.
new_text: At the beginning of the match, and of each innings, the umpire at the bowler’s wicket shall call “Play”; from that time no trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.

old_text: The wicket shall be held to be "down" when either of the bails is struck off, or if both bails be off, when a stump is struck out of the ground.
new_text: The wicket shall be held to be “down” when either of the bails is struck off, or, if both bails be off, when a stump is struck out of the ground.

old_text: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the striker’s bat or person:—
new_text: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the striker’s bat or person—“Bowled.”

old_text: Or, if the ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand, but not the wrist, be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher:—
new_text: Or, if the ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand, but not the wrist, be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher:—“Caught.”

old_text: Or, if in playing at the ball, providing it be not touched by the bat or hand, the striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball or with the hand or arm, with ball in hand:—
new_text: Or, if in playing at the ball, provided it be not touched by the bat or hand, the striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball or with hand or arm, with ball in hand:—“Stumped.”

old_text: Or, if with any part of his person he stop the ball, which, in the opinion of the umpire at the bowler’s wicket, shall have been pitched in a straight line from it to the striker’s wicket and would have hit it—“Leg before wicket.”
new_text: Or, if with any part of his person he stop the ball, which in the opinion of the umpire at the bowler’s wicket shall have been pitched in a straight line from it to the striker’s wicket and would have hit it:—“Leg before Wicket.”

old_text: Or if in playing at the ball he hit down his wicket with his bat or any part of his person or dress.—"Hit wicket.”
new_text: Or, if in playing at the ball he hit down his wicket with his bat or any part of his person or dress:—“Hit wicket.”

old_text: Or if under pretence of running, or otherwise, either of the batsmen wilfully prevent a ball from being caught—“Obstructing the field.”
new_text: Or, if under pretence of running, or otherwise, either of the batsmen wilfully prevent a ball from being caught:—“Obstructing the field.”

old_text: Or, if the ball be struck, or be struck by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat or any part of his person, except his hands;—“Hit the ball twice.”
new_text: Or, if the ball be struck, or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands:— “Hit the ball twice.”

old_text: If in running, or at any other time, while the ball is in play, he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman — “Run out.”
new_text: If in running, or at any other time, while the ball is in play, he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman:—“Run out.”

old_text: Or, if he touch with his hands or take up the ball while in play, unless at the request of the opposite side : — “Handled the ball.”
new_text: Or, if he touch with his hands or take up the ball while in play, unless at the request of the opposite side:—“Handled the ball.”

old_text: Or if he willfully obstruct any fieldsman : — “Obstructing the field."
new_text: Or, if he wilfully obstruct any fieldsman:—“Obstructing the field.”

old_text: After the ball shall have been finally settled, in the wicketkeeper’s or bowler’s hand it shall be “dead,” but when the bowler, is about to deliver the ball, if the batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said bowler may run him out, but if the bowler throw at that wicket and any run result it shall be scored “No ball.”
new_text: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the wicket-keeper’s or bowler’s hand it shall be “dead;” but when the bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said bowler may run him out; but if the bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “No-Ball.”

old_text: A batsman shall not retire from his wicket and return to it to complete his innings after another has been in, without the consent of the opposite side.
new_text: A batsman shall not retire from his wicket and return to it to complete his innings after another has been in without the consent of the opposite side.

old_text: A substitute shall be allowed to field or run between wickets for any player who may during the match be incapaciated from illness or injury, but for no other reason, except with the consent of the opposite side.
new_text: A substitute shall be allowed to field or run between wickets for any player who may during the match be incapacitated from illness or injury, but for no other reason, except with the consent of the opposite side.

old_text: In all cases where a substitute shall be allowed, the consent of the opposite side shall be obtained as to the person to act as substitute, and the place in the field which he shall take.
new_text: In all cases where a substitute shall be allowed, the consent of the opposite side shall be obtained as to the person to act as substitute and the place in the field which he shall take.

old_text: The fieldsman may stop the ball with any part of his person, but if he wilfully stop it otherwise, the ball shall be dead, and five runs added to the score; whatever runs may have been made, five only shall be added.
new_text: The fieldsman may stop the ball with any part of his person, but if he wilfully stop it otherwise the ball shall be “dead,” and five runs added to the score.

word_diff.old: score; whatever runs may have been made, five only shall be added.

old_text: The umpires are the sole judges of fair or unfair play, of the fitness of the ground, the weather, and the light for play; all disputes shall be determined by them, and if they disagree, the actual state of things shall continue.
new_text: The umpires are the sole judges of fair or unfair play, of the fitness of the ground, the weather, and the light for play; all disputes shall be determined by them, and if they disagree the actual state of things shall continue.

old_text: If the umpire at the bowler's end be not satisfied of the absolute fairness of the delivery of any ball, he shall call "No ball.”
new_text: If the umpire at the bowler’s end be not satisfied of the absolute fairness of the delivery of any ball, he shall call “No ball.” 48*.

old_text: On the last day of a match and in a one day match at any time, the in-side may declare their innings at any end.
new_text: On the last day of a match, or if a one- day match, at any time, the in-side shall be empowered to declare the innings at an end.

old_text: The umpire shall take especial care to call “No ball” instantly upon delivery, “Wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.

new_text: Prior to the commencement of a match it may be agreed that the over consists of 5 or 6 balls.

old_text: One wicket shall be pitched, as in Law 6, with a bowling stump opposite to it, at a distance of twenty-two yards.
new_text: One wicket shall be pitched, as in Law 6, with a bowling stump opposite to it, at a distance of 22 yards.

old_text: When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed twentytwo yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.
new_text: When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed 22 yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.

old_text: When there shall be less than five players on a side, neither byes, leg-byes, nor other throws shall be allowed, nor shall the striker be caught out behind the wicket, nor stumped.
new_text: When there shall be less than five players on a side neither byes, leg-byes, nor overthrows shall be allowed, nor shall the striker be caught out behind the wicket, nor stumped.

old_text: After the striker shall have made one run, if he start again he must touch the bowling stump or crease, and turn before the bail cross the ground to entitle him to another.
new_text: After the striker shall have made one run, if he start again he must touch the bowling stump or crease and turn before the ball cross the ground to entitle him to another.

old_text: The striker shall be entitled to three runs for lost ball, and the same number for ball wilfully stopped by a fieldsman, otherwise than with any part of his person.
new_text: The striker shall be entitled to three runs for lost ball, and the same number for ball wilfully stopped by a fieldsman otherwise than with any part of his person.

new_text: The umpire shall take especial care to call “No-ball” instantly upon delivery, “Wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.
